item.text: I have enough to draft the research account. I’m now consolidating the evidence into question-by-question dispositions, then I’ll append the machine records and the source disposition lists.

I did not assign a score.

**Orientation**
- AMLO had broad formal executive authority in 2022, but the economic picture was shaped by strong external constraints: post-pandemic recovery, inflation from global commodity and supply shocks, U.S. demand, and institutional checks from Banxico, Congress, courts, and autonomous bodies.
- The strongest 2022 evidence points to a mixed record: macro stability and social-protection spending were real strengths, while weak investment, high informality, and persistent inequality limited the case for durable prosperity.

**Evidence Index**
- [WEB-5B-001](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2022/02/oecd-economic-surveys-mexico-2022_a2937d37.html) | Macro stability with weak medium-term growth and high inequality | Matters because it frames the inherited baseline and the durability question.
- [WEB-5B-002](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2022/02/oecd-economic-surveys-mexico-2022_a2937d37.html) | Investment weakness, policy uncertainty, weak competition, and corruption constraints | Matters because it bears directly on fair economic rules and resistance to capture.
- [WEB-5B-003](https://www.imf.org/news/articles/2022/11/04/pr22373-imf-executive-board-concludes-2022-article-iv-consultation-with-mexico) | 2022 recovery, high inflation, neutral fiscal stance, and broad subsidies | Matters because it is the best single macro snapshot for 2022 shock management.
- [WEB-5B-004](https://www.gob.mx/shcp/prensa/comunicado-no-052-secretaria-de-hacienda-y-credito-publico-entrega-paquete-economico-2022-al-congreso) | 2022 budget priorities favored welfare, regional projects, and fiscal prudence | Matters because it shows the formal policy agenda.
- [WEB-5B-005](https://www.gob.mx/shcp/prensa/comunicado-no-9-informes-sobre-la-situacion-economica-las-finanzas-publicas-y-la-deuda-publica-al-cuarto-trimestre-de-2022) | End-2022 execution: stable debt, higher social protection, and higher physical investment | Matters because it tests whether budget priorities were actually carried out.
- [WEB-5B-006](https://www.coneval.org.mx/SalaPrensa/Comunicadosprensa/Documents/2023/Comunicado_07_Medicion_Pobreza_2022.pdf) | Poverty fell materially by 2022, but extreme poverty did not improve much | Matters because it is the clearest outcome measure for shared prosperity.
- [WEB-5B-007](https://www.gob.mx/shcp%7Cgacetaeconomica/articulos/la-tasa-de-referencia-banxico-aumento-a-6-00) | Banxico tightened sharply in 2022; year-end rates were much higher to fight inflation | Matters because it shows monetary-policy response to the inflation shock.
- [WEB-5B-008](https://www.dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle_popup.php?codigo=5637615) | Minimum wage rose 22% for 2022 | Matters because it is one of the main distributional policy moves.
- [WEB-5B-009](https://www.gob.mx/shcp/prensa/comunicado-no-37-presenta-el-secretario-de-hacienda-el-paquete-contra-la-inflacion-y-la-carestia) | PACIC launched as a broad anti-inflation package with price stabilization and fuel support | Matters because it shows the administration’s shock response.
- [WEB-5B-010](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2022/02/oecd-economic-surveys-mexico-2022_a2937d37.html) | Energy-policy uncertainty, weak competition, and slow anti-corruption implementation remained major obstacles | Matters because it is the strongest structural critique of capture and rule quality.

**Question Dispositions**
1. **5B.1 Broad and sustainable prosperity**: Mixed. The 2022 budget clearly prioritized social protection and infrastructure rather than overt patronage, and actual spending rose in those categories, but the growth/investment mix remained too weak to show a durable prosperity strategy. Records: WEB-5B-004, WEB-5B-005, WEB-5B-001.
2. **5B.2 Qualified economic leadership**: Mixed and only partially evidenced. The macro team and Banxico look technically competent, but I did not find strong 2022 appointment/removal evidence showing merit-based staffing decisions by the ruler himself. Record support is mostly indirect. Records: WEB-5B-003, WEB-5B-007, WEB-5B-010.
3. **5B.3 Macroeconomic stability**: Mostly yes. Fiscal policy stayed broadly neutral, debt remained stable, and Banxico tightened forcefully to contain inflation; the weakness is that inflation still ran hot. Records: WEB-5B-003, WEB-5B-005, WEB-5B-007.
4. **5B.4 Fair economic rules**: Weak to mixed. The formal budget and some anti-inflation steps were orderly, but OECD/IMF sources point to policy uncertainty in energy, weak competition, and regulatory burdens that discouraged investment. Records: WEB-5B-002, WEB-5B-010.
5. **5B.5 Resistance to economic capture**: Weak to mixed. There is evidence of anti-corruption rhetoric and some formal controls, but the structural evidence points to persistent capture risks, especially in energy and regulated sectors, with implementation lagging. Records: WEB-5B-002, WEB-5B-010.
6. **5B.6 Productive public investment**: Mixed. Public investment and physical investment rose, but OECD still described large infrastructure gaps and weak private investment, so the long-term payoff was not yet demonstrated. Records: WEB-5B-004, WEB-5B-005, WEB-5B-001, WEB-5B-002.
7. **5B.7 Evidence and correction**: Mixed. The government did publish data and adopted PACIC plus fuel support when inflation worsened, but the response was broad and partly untargeted rather than a clear evidence-led correction with fine-grained targeting. Records: WEB-5B-003, WEB-5B-009, WEB-5B-007.
8. **5B.8 Fair distribution**: Mixed. Poverty fell meaningfully, the minimum wage rose, and social protection spending increased, but extreme poverty barely improved, informality remained high, and OECD flagged women, youth, and poorer regions as especially affected. Records: WEB-5B-006, WEB-5B-008, WEB-5B-001, WEB-5B-003.
9. **5B.9 Managing economic shocks**: Moderately competent but blunt. The administration used price-support measures and Banxico tightened policy, which helped stabilize conditions, but inflation remained high and the measures were not especially targeted. Records: WEB-5B-003, WEB-5B-007, WEB-5B-009.
10. **5B.10 Lasting economic trajectory**: Mixed, leaning cautious. By 2022 the economy was stronger than the pandemic trough and poverty was lower, but weak investment, high informality, and unresolved regional inequality still limited the case that the ruler left a clearly stronger durable path. Records: WEB-5B-001, WEB-5B-002, WEB-5B-005, WEB-5B-006.

**Corroboration**
- OECD and IMF broadly agree that Mexico had macro stability but weak medium-term growth and elevated inflation.
- SHCP’s claimed fiscal prudence is broadly consistent with IMF/OECD characterizations of a cautious fiscal stance and stable debt.
- CONEVAL poverty results are based on INEGI ENIGH 2022, so the outcome record is methodologically anchored in official survey data.
- Banxico’s tightening is consistent with the inflation environment described by INEGI, IMF, and OECD.

**Reused Sources**
- OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022 is reused for macro-stability, investment weakness, competition, corruption, and long-run trajectory.
- SHCP fiscal releases are reused for both policy intent and actual fiscal execution.
- CONEVAL’s 2022 poverty release is reused for distribution, outcomes, and trajectory.
- Banxico material is reused for both shock response and macro stability.

**Uninspected Leads**
- INEGI ENIGH 2022 tabulations for more granular household, gender, and regional distribution.
- INEGI GDP annual release for the final 2022 growth estimate.
- Banxico SIE series for exact inflation and rate paths.
- ASF audits and sector-specific audits for procurement and project-quality evidence.
- World Bank Mexico overview and labor-market work for additional independent synthesis.

**Rejected**
- None in this pass.
- Some official self-justifying releases were treated as context rather than standalone proof when independent corroboration was available.

**Blocked**
- IMF eLibrary XML page for the 2022 Article IV report returned a 403 on direct open, so I relied on the press release snippet instead.
- A Banxico visual-summary page for late-2022 inflation/rate movements failed to open cleanly because of a Unicode decoding error, so I relied on the accessible Banxico snippets.

**Counts**
- Discovered sources: 10
- Opened/inspected sources: 6
- Accepted evidence records: 10
- Reused sources across multiple records: 4
- Rejected sources: 0
- Blocked sources: 2

**Remaining Questions**
- The main unresolved issue is attribution: how much of the poverty improvement came from wage policy, transfers, remittances, and the recovery itself.
- Another gap is personnel: I found little direct 2022 appointment evidence showing merit-based economic staffing decisions.
- More research would likely add detail, but not overturn the broad picture: stable macro management, stronger distributional support than many expected, and still-weak structural investment and productivity.
